title: Event-name vocabulary
description: The structured-log vocabulary defined in The Software Field Guide, "observability-engineering": which event names exist must be a queryable fact, so the vocabulary is versioned like code and reviewed on a cadence. This schema mirrors the shape rules of the Rego validator (policies/obs); the validator additionally enforces the semantic rules a JSON schema cannot — event names must be unique, and the review date must not be in the future or more than 365 days stale.

version.description: Version stamp of the vocabulary of record, bumped by whoever last changed it.

reviewedOn.description: The date of the last review, YYYY-MM-DD. Must name a real calendar date, not lie in the future, and be at most 365 days before the validation date.

events.description: The event names that exist. High-cardinality facts (order ids, request ids) belong in the event payload, never in a metric label — the vocabulary governs names only.

name.description: The event name, e.g. order.placed. Must be unique across the vocabulary.

description.description: What the event means — the one-sentence definition other teams rely on.
